item.title: What we know about Pope Leo XIV's planned lung operation this week
item.description:
Pope Leo said Sunday tests had discovered a nodule in his lung , which he will have removed surgically this week. The big picture: The first American pontiff , aged 71, is less than 18 months into a papacy that has been defined by public stances at odds with the White House , including clashes over immigration and deep skepticism about AI. What he's saying: "Dear friends, during some recent medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung. It was detected at a very early stage and is well localized. The doctors believe surgery is appropriate," the pope said during public remarks, per a translation from the Vatican. "Following their advice, I have therefore decided to undergo an operation to remove it. The operation is already scheduled for the coming days. I thank you for your spiritual closeness and entrust myself to your prayers." The pope did not explicitly say the…

item.title: Houthi missile attack targets Saudi capital Riyadh for third day in a row
item.description:
Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences Why are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through? Saudi Arabia has been forced to suspend all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh until next Saturday after a further round of Houthi missile attacks caused more damage and left one person dead. Some airlines, including Gulf Air and Bahrain Air, had already said they were cancelling flights until next Saturday. More missiles were fired at Saudi Arabian cities by the Houthis on Monday, Saudi Arabian’s military spokesperson said. The Gulf nation announced it was suspending flights from Riyadh, its second busiest airport, after Houthi missiles killed 13 people on Saturday and left more than 300 injured. item.title: Congratulations to the Hoover Institution's Robert E. Hall, on His Economics Nobel Prize
item.description:
Robert E. Hall, on the right. From Hoover's post today (and see also our colleague John Cochrane's post about Hall's work ): Robert E. Hall , the Robert and Carole McNeil Endowed Professor in Economics and Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution, Emeritus, and emeritus professor of economics in the School of Humanities and Sciences, is the recipient of the 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences. Hall was recognized with the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel for his contributions to the "microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization," alongside economist Michael Woodford, with whom he will share the approximately $1.2 million prize. item.title: Iran war live: Trump says Houthis ‘misbehaving’ as Riyadh flights halted
item.description:
President Donald Trump keeps pointing the finger at everyone for surging fuel prices but himself. Over the weekend, he once again blamed Ukraine, asserting that the country’s retaliatory airstrikes on Russia’s oil refineries were causing prices to spike. Now Trump is urging Ukraine to scrap its leader. “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does,” Trump said Saturday, suggesting that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to broker a peace deal with Russia. For weeks, Trump has called on Zelenskyy to stop striking Russia’s energy infrastructure, claiming that the attacks are “ hurting the world ,” while saying virtually nothing about Russia’s strikes against Ukraine. item.title: Susan Collins-Aligned Super PAC Buys Attack Ads in Portland... Oregon
item.description:
A Republican-affiliated super PAC is having a little trouble finding Maine on a map. The Defending Main Street super PAC spent thousands of dollars on an attack ad to audiences thousands of miles away from the Maine Senate race it was targeting. The ad hit Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson on the issue of taxes and cost of living in the state. “Maine can’t afford Troy Jackson and all his taxes,” the ad said. “It’s clear these people don’t know anything about Maine.” The group, which describes itself as the “most effective independent expenditure organization supporting the governing wing of the Republican Party,” paid for the ad to attack Jackson, who’s mounting a challenge to incumbent GOP Sen. item.title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
item.description:
Ann & Gordon Longridge and Matt de Neef (feature image) Venture out to Melbourne’s hilly east on any given day and there’s a good chance you’ll come across Ann Longridge. Pedalling slowly but steadily on her flatbar Liv, usually covered head to toe, she cuts a distinctive figure despite her short stature. And once you notice her, you’ll keep noticing her – sometimes riding on her own, sometimes with her husband Gordon, other times in a larger group. Out on the bike almost every single day. I first came across Ann back in August 2020, via an automated email from Strava. “There it goes!” read the email. “Ann Longridge nabbed your Local Legend title.” Seeing her profile picture was a lightbulb moment – so this was the rider I was seeing out on the roads of Ringwood East several times a week while I was training up for an Everesting .
